Title: Two-Factor Authentication Setup
<untrusted_retrieved_context id="chunk_2">
FAQ: How do I set up two-factor authentication?

Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security to your account. To enable 2FA, go to Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication and click Enable. We support authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy) and SMS verification. Authenticator apps are recommended over SMS for stronger security. After enabling 2FA, you will be prompted for a verification code at each login.

Title: Multi-Factor Authentication
<untrusted_retrieved_context id="chunk_1">
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is a security process that requires a user to provide two or more authentication factors to access a system, network, or application. The most common factors are something you know (like a password), something you have (like a smart card), and something you are (like a biometric).

MFA adds an extra layer of security by making it more difficult for attackers to gain access to a system. It is commonly used in enterprise environments to protect sensitive data and systems.
</untrusted_retrieved_context>
